facts.text: Flint Creek features the historic Hildebrand-Beck Mill, a grist mill listed on the National Register of Historic Places since 1972.
Native American tribes, primarily the Cherokee and Delaware peoples, inhabited the Flint Creek area beginning in the early nineteenth century.
Prehistoric archaeological sites in Flint Creek show that Archaic and Woodland peoples lived here over two thousand years ago.
Flint Creek is a spring-fed waterway that originates in Arkansas and flows southwest before joining the Illinois River.
Rolling hills and lush forests characterize the landscape of Flint Creek, which sits at an elevation of eleven hundred seventy-one feet.
Cherty limestone and dolomite formations underlay the hills and valleys of Flint Creek, influencing the local drainage patterns.
